concerns.text: FR-004 states the scoring model must be 'fine-tuned on a small set of expert-rated examples' (implied by 'without fine-tuning' contradiction or missing detail). The Idea explicitly requires a 'frozen, small-scale LLM... fine-tuned on a small set of expert-rated examples' to simulate the panel. The spec text 'without fine-tuning' in FR-004 contradicts the Idea's methodology and the Constitution (Principle VI) which mandates preserving raw semantic output to detect 'false certainty'. If the model is truly frozen without fine-tuning, it may lack the calibration to distinguish 'rigid' vs 'creative' responses as required. Clarify if the model is pre-fine-tuned (frozen during inference) or if the 'without fine-tuning' clause refers to the inference phase only.

US-2 Independent Test requires correlation >0.6 with a 'gold standard'. The Idea mentions 'Human-in-the-Loop Scoring' using a proxy model 'fine-tuned on a small set of expert-rated examples'. The spec does not explicitly define the source or size of this 'gold standard' set in the requirements, only in the test scenario. To ensure the 'frozen' model is actually calibrated as per the Idea, the spec should explicitly require the creation/validation of this gold-standard set (e.g., 'System MUST validate the proxy model against a manually curated set of N=50 expert-rated responses'). Without this, the 'frozen' model might be uncalibrated, invalidating the hypothesis test.
